components.name: Integrated Development Environment (IDE)
components.description: The software environment where code is written and tested—an attack surface due to risks like malicious extensions, insecure settings, or credential exposure.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Code Assistant Plugin
components.description: A compromised or intentionally malicious AI-powered IDE plugin that appears to assist with coding but performs unauthorized actions—introducing risks such as data exfiltration, credential harvesting, backdoor insertion, or manipulation of code and outputs.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Authentication Service
components.description: The service for verifying the identity of a user or system—risks include credential theft, weak authentication mechanisms, and session hijacking.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Authorization Service
components.description: The service for determining what an authenticated user or system is allowed to access or perform—risks include excessive permissions, privilege escalation, and misconfigured access controls.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Third Party MCP Server
components.description: An organization-operated MCP server that integrates the assistant with internal third-party services. Poses risks if misconfigured or inadequately secured, including unauthorized data access, insecure API exposure, and privilege escalation through service integrations.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Code Assistant Agent
components.description: The agent embedded within the Code Assistant Plugin and running inside the IDE on the developer's workstation. Modeled as a static component prior to plugin activation; once activated it becomes an actor with agency. Handles low-latency tasks such as inline completions and prompt assembly, and invokes local MCP servers for context retrieval. Subject to prompt injection, supply chain compromise via the plugin delivery path, and abuse of IDE-accessible APIs.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Remote Code Assistant Agent (remote, dynamic)
components.description: The agent (remote, dynamic) hosted entirely within the External SaaS trust boundary, opaque to the developer beyond its API surface. Remote: the agent and its agentic framework operate outside the developer's workstation within a third-party platform. Dynamic: the agent can take autonomous actions — tool calling, invoking MCP servers, and orchestrating multi-step workflows. May access additional tools, skills, and connectors not enumerated in this use case. Susceptible to prompt injection via remote context, third-party data handling risks, and limited developer visibility into its internal operations.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Remote Code Assistant Model
components.description: The core AI model that generates responses or code suggestions, run remotely (e.g., a cloud-hosted model such as a 30B-parameter model). Relevant in threat modeling due to risks like prompt injection, data leakage, model manipulation, and insecure output generation. This is a component within the Agent.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Remote RAG
components.description: A component, hosted remotely, that dynamically fetches relevant content from available data sources to augment the model's context and improve response quality. Introduces risks around ingestion of untrusted or manipulated content, exposure of sensitive data through retrieval, and injection of malicious inputs that propagate into model outputs.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Remote Context Store
components.description: A remotely hosted data store that supplies structured or unstructured content to the model or retrieval pipeline to enrich responses. Risks include unauthorized access to sensitive stored content, poisoning of the data corpus, and data leakage via model outputs.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: MCP Gateway
components.description: The ingress service (e.g., proxy, API gateway, or firewall) that receives and routes inbound connections to the assistant backend. Acts as a perimeter trust boundary—misconfiguration or compromise can expose backend infrastructure to unauthorized access or traffic manipulation.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: MCP Server — Agentic SaaS
components.description: The MCP server component hosted within the Agentic SaaS platform, responsible for exposing assistant capabilities and orchestrating downstream agent, model, and retrieval components. A high-value target due to its central role—risks include unauthorized access, data interception, and abuse of its broad orchestration capabilities.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: External Plugin Marketplace
components.description: An externally operated third-party platform where developers discover and install IDE plugins or extensions—introduces supply chain risks such as malicious or vulnerable plugins, insufficient vetting, and potential for unauthorized data access or exfiltration.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Agentic SaaS
components.description: An externally operated platform that delivers agentic assistant capabilities as a managed service. Introduces risks related to third-party data handling, limited visibility into model behavior and data flows, dependency on external availability, and reduced control over security posture.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: MCP Server — Cloud Service
components.description: An externally operated MCP server through which the assistant reaches an external service over the MCP protocol (e.g., GitHub, Slack, a database). The specific service is not scoped; it is characterized only by its MCP interface and by being external. Introduces supply chain risks including vulnerable or malicious dependencies, excessive permissions, and potential exfiltration of data passed through the integration.

externalReferences.comment: This component as declared in the system BOM.

components.name: Cloud Service (e.g., GitHub, Slack, database)
components.description: The external service that sits behind the MCP Server and is called remotely on behalf of the assistant (e.g., GitHub, Slack, a database). The specific service is intentionally not scoped; it is characterized only by being external and reachable through an MCP interface. Introduces additional risks including supply chain vulnerabilities, data exposure, and limited visibility or control over security practices.

useCases.name: Code Assistant — Sub Use Case 1b (External SaaS Agentic Framework)
useCases.description: The agentic framework is offloaded to an external SaaS platform, which hosts the dynamic agent, model, RAG pipeline, and context store behind an MCP Gateway. The workstation retains the Code Assistant Plugin and local agent. MCP Servers connect to both internal third-party services and external cloud platforms. The Plugin Marketplace is the source for plugin installation.
preconditions: The Code Assistant Plugin is installed from the External Plugin Marketplace and is authenticated.
The Agentic SaaS platform is accessible and the developer's account is provisioned.
The MCP Gateway on the Agentic SaaS platform is reachable from the developer's workstation.
Internal MCP Server and relevant Third Party Services (e.g., Jira, GitHub) are reachable.
External Cloud MCP Server is reachable if cloud service integrations are required.
postconditions: Developer receives AI-generated code suggestions produced by the remotely hosted model.
Developer code and context submitted to the SaaS platform are governed by the platform's data handling and retention policies.
Agent tool invocations on the SaaS side are logged by the platform.

exceptions.name: Agentic SaaS Platform Unavailable
exceptions.condition: The Agentic SaaS platform or MCP Gateway is unreachable due to an outage or network failure.
exceptions.description: The developer cannot complete multi-step agentic tasks; the plugin degrades to static-only responses.
exceptions.handling: The Code Assistant Agent (local, dynamic) notifies the developer of the degraded state and provides best-effort responses without SaaS delegation.

exceptions.name: Malicious Plugin from Marketplace
exceptions.condition: A plugin installed from the External Plugin Marketplace contains malicious code.
exceptions.description: The plugin exfiltrates developer credentials, codebase content, or manipulates agent outputs.
exceptions.handling: The Authentication and Authorization Services should enforce least-privilege; organizations should vet plugins prior to installation and monitor plugin network activity.

exceptions.name: Data Exfiltration via SaaS
exceptions.condition: Code or context submitted to the Agentic SaaS platform is accessed or retained in violation of data handling agreements.
exceptions.description: Sensitive proprietary code or secrets are exposed to the SaaS provider or third parties.
exceptions.handling: Organizations should review SaaS data retention policies, apply code redaction where possible, and avoid submitting secrets or regulated data to external platforms.

exceptions.name: Prompt Injection via Remote Context Store
exceptions.condition: Malicious content ingested into the Remote Context Store or Remote RAG pipeline redirects the remote agent's behavior.
exceptions.description: An injected instruction overrides the developer's intent, potentially causing unauthorized tool invocations or data exfiltration from the SaaS platform.
exceptions.handling: The SaaS platform and agentic framework apply input sanitization; suspicious instructions are flagged and execution is halted pending developer review.

successCriteria: Developer receives accurate code suggestions from the remote model within acceptable latency.
All data transmitted to the Agentic SaaS platform is governed by agreed data handling policies.
Agent tool calls are restricted to permitted internal and external MCP Servers.
Plugin integrity is verified prior to installation and during runtime.
notes: This sub use case introduces a third-party trust boundary at the Agentic SaaS platform, which hosts the most capable (e.g., 30B-parameter) model.
The External Plugin Marketplace is a supply chain risk vector — plugins should be vetted and sourced from trusted publishers.
MCP Gateway acts as the sole ingress point to the SaaS agentic stack and is a high-value target.

persona.label: External attacker
persona.description: An individual outside the organization who publishes a look-alike of the official Code Assistant Plugin to a plugin marketplace.

weaknesses.name: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
weaknesses.description: The IDE installs plugin code from a marketplace without verifying its publisher signature or integrity against a trusted source.

weaknesses.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
weaknesses.description: Plugin code supplied by an external marketplace runs inside the IDE with access to the local codebase and credentials.

zones.name: Internal
zones.description: Represents locally networked resources: the developer's workstation, the IDE, the Code Assistant Plugin and its embedded agent, the local agentic framework, and any MCP servers reachable within the organization's local network. All components within this boundary are subject to the organization's own security controls.

zones.name: External SaaS
zones.description: Represents remotely networked managed services: the Agentic SaaS platform (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor), the External Plugin Marketplace, and any third-party application services accessed over the public internet. Components within this boundary operate under a third-party trust model with limited organizational visibility.

zones.name: External Cloud
zones.description: Represents remotely networked external services that the assistant reaches through an MCP Server interface. These services are characterized only by the MCP protocol and by being external, for example GitHub, Slack, or a database; the specific services are intentionally not scoped. Components within this zone are governed by the external service provider's own security and shared-responsibility model.

persona.description: Human actor who writes, modifies, and maintains code—considered a potential target (e.g., phishing, credential theft) or source of risk (e.g., introducing vulnerabilities or misconfigurations).

actors.description: The human developer who interacts with the code assistant within the IDE.

Dynamic: the agent can take autonomous actions — tool calling, invoking MCP servers, and orchestrating multi-step workflows. May access additional tools, skills, and connectors not enumerated in this use case. Susceptible to prompt injection via remote context, third-party data handling risks, and limited developer visibility into its internal operations.

flows.name: Plugin Marketplace delivers plugin to IDE
flows.description: The External Plugin Marketplace delivers the Code Assistant Plugin to the developer's IDE during installation. Applies to Sub Use Case 1b only.

flows.name: Developer submits coding request
flows.description: The Developer initiates a coding assistance interaction by submitting a request through the IDE.

flows.name: IDE activates plugin
flows.description: The IDE routes the developer's request to the Code Assistant Plugin.

flows.name: Plugin authenticates developer
flows.description: The Code Assistant Agent sends credentials to the Authentication Service to verify developer identity.

flows.name: Plugin checks developer permissions
flows.description: The Code Assistant Agent queries the Authorization Service to verify developer permissions.

flows.name: Local agent forwards request to MCP Gateway
flows.description: The Code Assistant Agent sends complex tasks to the MCP Gateway on the Agentic SaaS platform for remote execution. Applies to Sub Use Case 1b only.

flows.name: MCP Gateway routes request to SaaS MCP Server
flows.description: The MCP Gateway authenticates the inbound request and routes it to the MCP Server — Agentic SaaS.

flows.name: SaaS MCP Server dispatches to remote agent
flows.description: The MCP Server — Agentic SaaS dispatches the request to the Remote Code Assistant Agent within the Agentic SaaS platform.

flows.name: Remote agent invokes remote model
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Agent sends the enriched prompt to the Remote Code Assistant Model for inference.

flows.name: Remote agent queries remote RAG
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Agent retrieves augmented context from the Remote RAG pipeline.

flows.name: Remote agent reads remote context store
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Agent fetches structured context from the Remote Context Store.

flows.name: Remote agent calls internal MCP Server
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Agent issues a tool call to the internal Third Party MCP Server (e.g., Jira, GitHub) via a secure channel. Applies to Sub Use Case 1b only.

flows.name: Remote dynamic agent calls cloud MCP Server
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Agent invokes the MCP Server — Cloud Service to interact with an external service over MCP (e.g., GitHub, Slack, a database). Applies to Sub Use Case 1b only.

flows.name: Cloud MCP Server calls cloud service
flows.description: The MCP Server — Cloud Service forwards the tool call to the target Cloud Service (e.g., GitHub, Slack, a database) and returns results.

flows.name: Remote model returns response to developer
flows.description: The Remote Code Assistant Model response travels back through the MCP Gateway and Code Assistant Plugin to the Developer in the IDE.

attackPatterns.name: Malicious Software Download
attackPatterns.description: An attacker uses deceptive methods to cause a user or an automated process to download and install dangerous code.

attackPatterns.name: Install Malicious Extension
attackPatterns.description: An adversary directly installs or tricks a user into installing a malicious extension into existing trusted software.

threats.name: Malicious look-alike Code Assistant Plugin installed from a marketplace
threats.description: Developer uses an unofficial marketplace and unknowingly installs a malicious version of the official plugin into the IDE. This results in code being sent to an external, attacker-controlled backend.

threatScenarios.name: Developer installs a look-alike plugin that sends the codebase to an attacker
threatScenarios.description: Developer uses an unofficial marketplace and unknowingly installs a malicious version of the official plugin into the IDE. This results in code being sent to an external, attacker-controlled backend.
threatScenarios.event: The look-alike plugin is delivered to the IDE over flow:1b:marketplace-to-plugin and activated.

likelihood.rationale: Look-alike extensions appear regularly on public marketplaces; success needs the developer to pick the wrong listing.

attackPaths.name: Marketplace listing to code exfiltration
attackPaths.objective: Exfiltrate proprietary code from the developer workstation

steps.name: Publish look-alike
steps.description: Attacker publishes a plugin that imitates the official Code Assistant Plugin.

steps.name: Deliver to IDE
steps.description: The developer installs the look-alike and the marketplace delivers it to the IDE.

steps.name: Exfiltrate
steps.description: The plugin reads the open codebase through IDE APIs and posts it to an attacker-controlled backend.

controls.name: Verify plugin publisher signature before install
controls.description: The IDE refuses to install a Code Assistant Plugin unless it is signed by the expected publisher key.

controls.name: Allow-list approved plugin marketplaces and publishers
controls.description: Only plugins from approved marketplaces and publisher IDs can be installed, enforced by IDE policy.

controls.name: Run AI plugins with restricted file and network access
controls.description: The plugin runs in a sandbox that limits which files it can read and which hosts it can reach, and its egress is monitored.

damageScenarios.name: Proprietary code exposed to an attacker

impacts.description: Loss of intellectual property and of any secrets in the codebase.

risks.name: Proprietary code exfiltrated through a look-alike plugin
risks.statement: An external attacker (source) gets a developer to install a look-alike Code Assistant Plugin (event), which sends proprietary code to an attacker-controlled backend (impact).

inherentRisk.rationale: No publisher signature check or marketplace allow-list is assumed.
